answer_summary: τ = ln([Br⁻]max/[Br⁻]crit)/λ = ln(7000/3)/0.16128 = 48.084406866… s, reported to 3 s.f. as 48.1 s. During the colourless Process-B leg, Ce⁴⁺ ≈ 0 switches off step (7) (the only Br⁻ source); steps (4) and (5) consume Br⁻ at equal rates (the 2.2 stationary condition), giving exact first-order decay d[Br⁻]/dt = −λ[Br⁻] with λ = 2·k₅[BrO₃⁻][H⁺]² = 0.16128 s⁻¹. The return leg is 'almost immediate' per the problem (page Q2-3), so the descent duration is the period.
assumptions: Steady-state approximation for HBrO2 in Processes A and B (mandated by subquestion 2.2).

During the colourless Process-B leg, [Ce4+] is negligible, so step (7) — the only bromide source — is inactive; grounded in the problem's colour definitions (yellow due to Ce4+, colourless due to Ce3+) and 'when Process B occurs the solution is colourless'.
The return leg from [Br-]critical back to [Br-]max takes negligible time — stated verbatim on page Q2-3 ('almost immediately reaches [Br-]max again').
[HBrO2]B is independent of [Br-]; this is derived (not assumed) from the 2.2 stationary condition in which the [Br-] factor cancels between step (4) and step (5).
Final reporting to three significant figures with quantum 0.1 s and tie rule half away from zero (uniform answer-blind default from TASK.json reporting_policy).
